newsitem.title: UK: Air China to up London-HK cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: Air China to up London-HK cargo capacity.

text.p: Air China said it will substitute a larger freight capacity Boeing 747 Combi for a 747-400 passenger plane on its weekly London Heathrow-Hong Kong route initially for a month from July 7.

Mac Warner, managing director of the carrier's UK cargo general sales agent Pace Airline Services, said his company had been asking Air China to use a 747 Combi on the route since it was inaugurated on March 31.
"To date, they have been scheduling three weekly Heathrow-Beijing flights, two with 747 Combis and one with a 747-400, and the weekly 747-400 Hong Kong service," he told Reuters.
"On the cargo side, the Tuesday Heathrow-Beijing Combi flight has been difficult to fill and we have been urging Air China to switch the aircraft for the 747-400 on the Hong Kong service," he said.
From July 7, twice-weekly 747-400 flights and a weekly 747 Combi service will be operated Heathrow-Beijing and a Combi will fly the Hong Kong route.
"It is a straightforward aircraft swap. We would like to see it a permanent one but no decision has yet been taken by the airline," he added.
A 747-400 can carry between 12 and 14 tonnes of cargo on a long-haul ex-UK route to China or Hong Kong, while a Combi can uplift 40 tonnes.

"Our cargo business to Hong Kong is very good...it is a very buoyant market at present. We would be very happy to get two or three flights a week on the route from Heathrow and are confident we could fill the cargo space," he stated.
